whatIs.title: What is useState?
whatIs.description: useState is a built-in React Hook that allows you to add state to function components.
whatIs.content: In React, component state refers to data that changes over time and affects component rendering. The useState Hook is React's way of managing state in function components. It returns a state value and a function to update that state.

rules.title: Rules of Use
rules.description: Important rules to follow when using useState.

rule1.title: Only Call at the Top Level
rule1.content: Don't call useState inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.

rule2.title: Only Call from React Functions
rule2.content: Only call useState from React function components or custom Hooks.

rule3.title: State Updates are Asynchronous
rule3.content: After calling the state setter, the state doesn't change immediately. React batches updates for better performance.

rule4.title: State Updates Trigger Re-renders
rule4.content: Each call to the state setter causes the component to re-render (if the state value actually changed).

practice1.title: Use Multiple State Variables
practice1.content: Manage related but independent state separately instead of putting them in one large object.

practice2.title: Avoid Unnecessary State
practice2.content: If a value can be calculated from existing props or state, don't create separate state for it.

practice3.title: Use Functional Updates
practice3.content: When new state depends on old state, use functional updates to ensure correctness.

practice4.title: Name State Variables Descriptively
practice4.content: Use descriptive names like [isLoading, setIsLoading] instead of [flag, setFlag].

commonMistakes.title: Common Mistakes
commonMistakes.description: Common pitfalls to avoid when using useState.

mistake1.title: Directly Mutating State
mistake1.content: Never directly modify state objects or arrays; always create new copies.

mistake2.title: Calling Setters During Render
mistake2.content: Don't call state setters directly in the component's render logic, as this causes infinite loops.

whatIs.title: What is useMemo?
whatIs.description: useMemo is a React Hook that memoizes calculated values to avoid expensive computations on every render.
whatIs.content: useMemo accepts a create function and a dependency array, and only recalculates the value when dependencies change. This is particularly useful for performance optimization, especially when computations are expensive.

syntax.title: Basic Syntax
syntax.param1: Calculation function - returns the value you want to memoize
syntax.param2: Dependency array - only recalculate when these values change

scenario1.title: Expensive Calculations
scenario1.content: When you have computationally intensive operations in your component, useMemo can avoid repeated calculations on every render.

scenario2.title: Referential Equality
scenario2.content: When you need to pass objects or arrays in dependency arrays, useMemo can maintain referential equality.

scenario3.title: Optimize Child Component Rendering
scenario3.content: When used with React.memo, useMemo can prevent unnecessary child component re-renders.

reference.title: Referential Equality
reference.name: Name
reference.note: Note: Without useMemo, a new object is created on every render, even if values haven't changed.

vsUseCallback.description: Understand the difference between useMemo and useCallback.

practice1.title: Don't Overuse
practice1.content: Not all values need useMemo. Only use it when calculations are truly expensive or referential equality matters.

practice2.title: Set Dependencies Correctly
practice2.content: Ensure the dependency array includes all values used in the calculation function.

practice3.title: Measure Performance
practice3.content: Measure performance before and after adding useMemo to ensure it actually provides improvement.

commonMistakes.title: Common Mistakes
commonMistakes.description: Pitfalls to avoid when using useMemo.

mistake1.title: Premature Optimization
mistake1.content: Don't use useMemo where there's no performance problem; it makes code more complex.

mistake2.title: Missing Dependencies
mistake2.content: Ensure all variables used in the calculation function are in the dependency array.

mistake3.title: Empty Dependency Array
mistake3.content: If the dependency array is empty, the value is only calculated once, which may lead to stale values.
